Therefore, an additional spouse may be ineligible for permission through the same polygamous relationship even where the marriage was legally conducted abroad. 6. Marriages where a previous relationship has not permanently ended Applicants and their partners must generally demonstrate that any previous marriage, civil partnership or qualifying durable relationship has permanently broken down. Someone who remains legally married to another person, without the previous relationship having ended in a way recognised by law, may encounter difficulties qualifying for a new spouse visa. item.title: Senate probes Tansian University over alleged violations
item.description: — Akpabio warns erring public, private universities — NUC reform bill scales second reading By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has ordered an investigation into the operations and management of Tansian University, Umunya, Anambra State, over allegations of administrative excesses and concerns about its compliance with regulatory requirements of the National Universities Commission (NUC). The Senate, at plenary on Thursday, referred the matter to its Committee on Tertiary Education and TETFund, directing it to investigate the allegations and report back within two weeks. The resolution followed a motion by Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central, who raised concerns about the university’s alleged disregard for established regulatory procedures, particularly in the appointment and dismissal of personnel. President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, directed the committee to conduct the probe, warning that public and private universities found to have violated the law must be brought to order. Akpabio stressed the need to strengthen the regulatory authority of the NUC to ensure that universities operate within the law. He said the National Assembly had an oversight responsibility to support the commission in enforcing standards across the university system. The Senate President added that where an institution was found to have violated the law, the National Assembly could recommend appropriate action to the President, including the proscription of the university. item.title: Paramilitary recruitment portal opens October 28

Although no case of Ebola has been confirmed in any state in the zone, authorities said they were strengthening disease surveillance, alerting health workers and border teams, and improving emergency response capacity to contain any potential outbreak. The measures include heightened monitoring of suspected cases, public health awareness campaigns, infection prevention and control, and preparations to isolate and manage suspected cases. Abia races to prepare isolation centres, seeks funds for protective gear Abia State Government said it had begun emergency preparedness measures against a possible Ebola outbreak, including plans to equip isolation facilities, procure personal protective equipment and intensify disease surveillance. The Permanent Secretary of the Abia State Ministry of Health, Dr Blossom Uma-Kalu, who disclosed this in an interview with Vanguard, assured residents that no case of Ebola had been recorded in the state. Uma-Kalu said the ministry had initiated consultations involving relevant departments and agencies to assess the state’s preparedness and identify gaps requiring urgent intervention. She, however, said additional funding was needed to procure personal protective equipment, PPE, thermometers, hand sanitisers and other essential supplies. According to her, the state was preparing a budget to determine which needs could be met through federal support and which would require state funding. “We have held meetings following communication from the Federal Ministry of Health about the case in Abuja. Health workers and relevant public health teams have been alerted to maintain a high index of suspicion,” she said. The Permanent Secretary said the government was also considering an additional isolation facility, while work continued on existing centres. She disclosed that the Infectious Disease Hospital (IDH) in Aba was nearing completion, while the isolation facility at a specialist hospital in Umuahia was undergoing remodelling. According to her, the state was also assessing a proposed facility that could be adapted for isolation if necessary. Uma-Kalu explained that establishing isolation centres required trained personnel, adequate funding and appropriate treatment and monitoring facilities, making it impractical to establish such centres in every local government area. She said the ministry was preparing a public health advisory to educate residents about Ebola, its symptoms and preventive measures. The advisory, she added, would include designated emergency telephone numbers for reporting suspected cases. Uma-Kalu urged health workers, particularly those in private hospitals and laboratories, to remain vigilant and pay attention to patients’ travel histories and symptoms that could suggest Ebola infection. She said public health teams working in communities and at entry points into the state had also been alerted to watch out for possible cases. The Permanent Secretary advised residents to remain calm but vigilant, avoid unnecessary contact with the blood and other body fluids of suspected cases, and observe appropriate infection-prevention measures. She cautioned against dismissing suspicious symptoms as ordinary malaria without proper medical assessment. “People should not be afraid, but they need to be vigilant. Health workers must maintain a high index of suspicion and ensure that cases with symptoms suggestive of Ebola are properly assessed,” she said. She urged residents to rely on verified public health information rather than panic, adding that the state was taking steps to prepare for any eventuality. Enugu intensifies surveillance across 17 LGAs Enugu State Government said it had intensified disease surveillance across its 17 local government areas and reactivated its Public Health Emergency Operations Centre following the reported Ebola case in the country. The Commissioner for Health, Prof. George O. Ugwu, who disclosed this in an interview with Vanguard, reassured residents that no case of Ebola Virus Disease had been confirmed in the state. “Let me begin by reassuring the people of Enugu State that there is currently no confirmed case of Ebola Virus Disease in Enugu State,” he said. Ugwu said the government was strengthening preparedness in collaboration with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Port Health Services, airport authorities and other relevant partners. He noted that Enugu’s position as a major travel and commercial hub, particularly through the Akanu Ibiam International Airport, made heightened surveillance necessary. According to him, surveillance had been reinforced across the state, while rapid response teams and technical personnel remained on standby to respond to suspected cases. The commissioner urged public and private health facilities to remain alert, promptly isolate suspected cases in line with established protocols and report them to the appropriate Disease Surveillance and Notification Officer (DSNO) or the state emergency operations centre. He also advised health workers to maintain strict infection prevention and control measures, including the use of appropriate protective equipment. Ugwu urged residents to remain calm, practise proper hand hygiene, avoid contact with the body fluids of sick persons and promptly report suspected cases to health authorities. He cautioned against rumours, misinformation and stigmatisation, advising the public to rely on verified information from the state Ministry of Health, the NCDC and other recognised health authorities. He assured residents that the government would continue working with relevant agencies to strengthen Ebola preparedness, surveillance and response. The Commissioner for Health, Dr Afam Ben Obidike, who disclosed this while briefing reporters in Awka, said the officers would screen passengers arriving in the state from Abuja, Lagos and other African countries. He urged residents not to panic, assuring them that the government was taking measures to prevent an outbreak. Obidike said the state had monitored 40 persons of interest, with 33 completing their monitoring period and being cleared, while seven remained under active follow-up. He said all seven were stable. According to him, Anambra had developed an Ebola preparedness and operational plan covering surveillance, rapid response, infection prevention and control, laboratory coordination, referral arrangements, risk communication and logistics. He added that the state’s surveillance network across the 21 local government areas, the airport, motor parks and other public places would be strengthened to ensure early detection and reporting. The commissioner said state surveillance officers had participated in a two-day online training organised by the NCDC on monitoring persons of interest. We also need a clearer explanation of how the woman entered the country and what happened after her arrival. “Where did she stay? Where did she go? How many people did she come into contact with?” he asked, stressing that these details were essential to establishing the extent of possible exposure and reassuring the public,” he queried. Tomori warned that the time taken to confirm the infection highlighted the need for healthcare workers to maintain a high index of suspicion when treating patients who have travelled from areas experiencing Ebola outbreaks. On the timeline, Tomori said the period was still within the incubation period. “However, the fact that it took until the 20th (October) to confirm the case is a concern and we need to improve on that. By the time the woman had moved between different locations, the opportunity for further exposure might already have arisen. “We faced a similar problem in 2014, when Patrick Sawyer arrived in Nigeria. It took about three or four days to diagnose him. Samples were initially being sent for malaria testing. When someone arrives from an area experiencing an outbreak, our level of awareness should be much higher. “The first disease that should come to mind is the one circulating in the area from which the person has travelled, not malaria, which is common in our environment. Our healthcare workers need to understand this. Their own lives are also at risk, so they must remain alert. “If I hear that someone has arrived from a country experiencing an Ebola outbreak, or from an area close to one, my first question would be whether the person could have Ebola before considering other possibilities. “We need to move beyond routine thinking before concluding that someone has malaria, healthcare workers should be up to date on diseases circulating in the places from which their patients have travelled,” he noted. On contact tracing Tomori said the health authorities need to gather more information and identify as many contacts as possible. “We should have more details than we currently have. For now, there is no reason to panic, the authorities are putting the necessary measures in place. What we need to do is prepare for the worst-case scenario. Suppose two or three of those contacts test positive. What happens next? “Do we have the hospitals, isolation facilities and other resources needed to manage additional cases? Those are the questions we should be asking now, rather than assuming that everyone will die because Ebola has entered the country. There are 44 people reportedly under quarantine. According to him, healthcare workers must look beyond common illnesses such as malaria when a patient’s travel history suggests possible exposure to a dangerous infectious disease. “When someone arrives from an area experiencing an outbreak, our level of awareness should be much higher. The first disease that should come to mind is the one circulating in the area from which the person has travelled, not malaria, which is common in our environment.” He warned that failure to recognise the possibility of Ebola early could expose healthcare workers and other patients to infection. “I think the authorities need to gather more information and identify as many contacts as possible. We should have more details than we currently have,” he said. He said Nigeria should plan for the worst-case scenario without creating unnecessary public alarm. “For now, there is no reason to panic. The authorities are putting the necessary measures in place,” he said, adding that preparedness would be critical if the outbreak expanded. Further, Tomori also cautioned against relying exclusively on geographical distance to assess Nigeria’s risk. He said although the World Health Organisation had reportedly classified the country as being at low risk, he argued that regular travel between Nigeria and affected regions needed to be considered. “Hundreds of Nigerians travel to the region for business and other activities before returning home. That makes the risk more complicated than simply measuring the distance between two locations,” he said. On the strain responsible for the outbreak, Tomori explained that Ebola viruses differ in their characteristics and severity, even though they belong to the same broader group. “The Zaire strain has recorded fatality rates approaching 90 per cent in some outbreaks, while the Sudan strain has recorded rates of around 60 per cent. Bundibugyo has recorded fatality rates of about 50 per cent in some outbreaks,” he said. He cautioned against interpreting the comparatively lower fatality rate as evidence that the strain was harmless. “When we say Bundibugyo is less severe, however, that does not mean it is harmless or that it cannot kill people,” he said. item.title: Reps pass bill for National Children’s Hospital in Imo
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina,Abuja The House of Representatives has passed for second reading a bill seeking to establish a National Children’s Hospital in Ideato, Imo State, to expand access to specialised paediatric healthcare and reduce child mortality in Nigeria. The bill, sponsored by the member representing Ideato North and South Federal Constituency, Ikenga Imo Ugochinyere, scaled the second-reading hurdle after lawmakers considered its general principles during plenary. Leading the debate, Ugochinyere said the proposed hospital would provide specialised medical services for children, strengthen the country’s capacity to manage complex childhood illnesses and improve access to quality healthcare. The lawmaker said the proposed legislation was in line with the constitutional responsibility of government to protect the welfare of citizens, particularly children, who remain among the most vulnerable members of society. He cited Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which provides that the security and welfare of the people shall be the primary purpose of government. According to him, the provision places an obligation on government to prioritise accessible, affordable and quality healthcare for Nigerians, including children. Ugochinyere also expressed concern over Nigeria’s child mortality burden, noting that preventable conditions such as malaria, pneumonia, diarrhoeal diseases and neonatal complications continue to threaten the survival and healthy development of children. He argued that a dedicated national paediatric hospital would improve the diagnosis and treatment of complex childhood diseases while supporting medical research, professional training and early intervention services. The lawmaker further referenced Section 13 of the Child Rights Act, 2003, which recognises every child’s right to the best attainable state of physical, mental and spiritual health. He said the proposed hospital would provide an institutional framework for advancing child-centred medical care and improving health outcomes. Drawing comparisons with specialised paediatric institutions in other countries, Ugochinyere cited Children’s National Hospital in Washington, D.C., United States, and the Red Cross War Memorial Children’s Hospital in Cape Town, South Africa. He said Nigeria needed to invest more deliberately in specialised healthcare facilities capable of delivering advanced treatment and life-saving interventions for children. The proposed hospital in Ideato is expected to serve children from Imo State, the South-East and other parts of the country, subject to its eventual capacity and service arrangements. item.title: IPOB member pleads guilty, jailed 20 years for belonging to proscribed group
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Federal High Court in Abuja, on Thursday, convicted and sentenced a self-confessed member of the Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB), Mr. Paul Okechukwu, 48, to 20 years in prison for belonging to a proscribed organisation. The defendant pleaded guilty to one count of a two-count charge the Federal Government preferred against him. The Federal Government alleged in the first count that the defendant, who is from Nnewi South in Anambra State, had in 2021, while in Imo State, committed an offence by belonging to IPOB, a proscribed organisation, contrary to and punishable under Section 16 of the Terrorism (Prevention) (Amendment) Act, 2013. In the second count, the Federal Government alleged that the defendant participated in an attack in which two security operatives were killed, and thereby committed an offence contrary to Section 2(1) of the Terrorism (Prevention) (Amendment) Act, 2013. After the charge was read to him, the defendant pleaded not guilty to the second count. In view of this development, and following an application by the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, who was in court to lead the prosecution, the court struck out the second count after it was withdrawn. Relying on Section 72 of the Terrorism Prevention and Prohibition Act (TPPA) 2022, the Attorney-General applied for the court to allow a witness from the Department of State Services (DSS) to review some facts of the case. The witness, whose name was given as “ABC” for the purpose of the trial, identified the defendant as a member of IPOB, which he said had since been outlawed. He told the court that the defendant was involved in acts of terrorism, which he said included attacks on security agents. The witness, who said he was part of a team that investigated the defendant, tendered a copy of the report, which was admitted as Exhibit A. While applying for the defendant to be convicted, the AGF argued that the law prescribed a minimum sentence of 20 years for the offence. “We therefore urge my lord to impose the maximum sentence, at least to serve as a deterrent to others and to also show that the nation cannot condone any act of terrorism,” the AGF added. Meanwhile, immediately after the AGF made the application, the defendant broke down in tears in the dock, begging the court to temper justice with mercy. Delivering judgment in the matter, Justice Hawa Yilwa found the defendant guilty and sentenced him to 20 years. The court said it took note of the charge against the defendant and “the ripple effect it has on the nation.” It held that the defendant should be remanded in any correctional facility chosen by the Comptroller-General of the Nigerian Correctional Service to serve his sentence, which should count from the day he was arrested. item.title: 2027: PRP alleges multi-million naira plot to break its ranks, sabotage opposition coalition
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) has alleged a plot by senior members of the ruling party to destabilise its ranks, sabotage its grassroots structures and undermine efforts to build a credible opposition coalition ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party said the alleged scheme involved hundreds of millions of naira to compromise its officials, exploit former members and create divisions capable of weakening its electoral fortunes. In a statement by its National Chairman, Dr. Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, the PRP alerted its members and the public to the alleged plot, warning supporters against inducements to work against the party. It alleged that some disgraced former members were being deployed to create the impression of internal division, while strategically placed party officers were being used to undermine its grassroots support. The PRP specifically warned against attempts by unauthorised persons to recruit polling agents in its name, urging members to resist and expose any financial inducements intended to divert their support. “The persons in the governing party involved in this scheme have been advised to steer clear of the PRP and distance themselves from attempts to create a fictional PRP with their party’s funds and their names,” the statement said. The party warned that serving officers found to be involved would face disciplinary action, insisting that neither financial inducements nor internal sabotage would make it abandon its political commitments. “The leadership of the PRP wishes to assure its candidates and Party supporters that it will not sacrifice their commitments and loyalty at any price,” Baba-Ahmed said. The PRP said it remained committed to challenging the continuation of the Tinubu administration beyond 2027 and playing a role in building a potentially winning opposition coalition. item.title: Terrorism: Court jails man 40 years for spying for late Benue militia leader
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja The Federal High Court in Abuja on Thursday convicted and sentenced a man, Sunday Frank, to 40 years in prison after he confessed that he served as a spy for an alleged notorious bandit leader in Benue State, Terwase Akwaza, popularly known as Gana. Gana, who reportedly began as part of a militia group defending Benue communities against attacks by suspected herdsmen, was killed in September 2020 by security operatives. In a four-count charge brought before the court by the federal government, it alleged that the convict, Frank, who hails from Katsina-Ala Local Government Area of Benue State, monitored and provided information to Gana about the movement of security agents. It alleged that the convict’s coverage for Gana spanned Benue and Taraba states. Specifically, in the charge, which was personally prosecuted by the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, it was alleged that the convict had also kidnapped one Samuel in 2022 and held him hostage until the sum of N40,000 was paid for his release. He was accused of committing offences contrary to sections 21 and 24 of the Terrorism Prevention and Prohibition Act (TPPA) 2022. Even though the defendant denied counts 1, 2 and 3 of the charge, which related to his alleged involvement in abduction, he pleaded guilty to count 4, which related to providing information to the Benue bandit leader. Following his plea, the AGF applied for the counts the defendant denied to be struck out, a request the court granted. Afterwards, the prosecution produced a witness who told the court that he was part of the team that investigated the defendant. He mounted the witness box and reviewed the facts of the case. The witness, simply identified as “AAA” after the court gave the FG permission to shield his real name, said the defendant had confessed to being a bandit and an informant to the late Gana. He said the defendant, who was arrested in 2022, admitted that aside from giving updates on the movement of security agents to Gana, he also confessed to his involvement in banditry and participation in the abduction of two persons. According to the witness, the defendant’s confessions were both oral and written. The FG’s application to tender the statement in evidence was not opposed by the defence lawyer, Mr Y. Y. Shullai. Consequently, trial judge Hawa Yilwa admitted and marked the defendant’s statement as Exhibit A. item.content:encoded: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja The Federal High Court in Abuja on Thursday convicted and sentenced a man, Sunday Frank, to 40 years in prison after he confessed that he served as a spy for an alleged notorious bandit leader in Benue State, Terwase Akwaza, popularly known as Gana. Gana, who reportedly began as part of a militia group defending Benue communities against attacks by suspected herdsmen, was killed in September 2020 by security operatives. In a four-count charge brought before the court by the federal government, it alleged that the convict, Frank, who hails from Katsina-Ala Local Government Area of Benue State, monitored and provided information to Gana about the movement of security agents. It alleged that the convict’s coverage for Gana spanned Benue and Taraba states. Specifically, in the charge, which was personally prosecuted by the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, it was alleged that the convict had also kidnapped one Samuel in 2022 and held him hostage until the sum of N40,000 was paid for his release. He was accused of committing offences contrary to sections 21 and 24 of the Terrorism Prevention and Prohibition Act (TPPA) 2022. Even though the defendant denied counts 1, 2 and 3 of the charge, which related to his alleged involvement in abduction, he pleaded guilty to count 4, which related to providing information to the Benue bandit leader. Following his plea, the AGF applied for the counts the defendant denied to be struck out, a request the court granted. Afterwards, the prosecution produced a witness who told the court that he was part of the team that investigated the defendant. He mounted the witness box and reviewed the facts of the case. The witness, simply identified as “AAA” after the court gave the FG permission to shield his real name, said the defendant had confessed to being a bandit and an informant to the late Gana. He said the defendant, who was arrested in 2022, admitted that aside from giving updates on the movement of security agents to Gana, he also confessed to his involvement in banditry and participation in the abduction of two persons. According to the witness, the defendant’s confessions were both oral and written. The FG’s application to tender the statement in evidence was not opposed by the defence lawyer, Mr Y. Y. Shullai. Consequently, trial judge Hawa Yilwa admitted and marked the defendant’s statement as Exhibit A. The witness further told the court that his team investigated the defendant’s activities and filed a report. The report was tendered and admitted as Exhibit B. In his submissions, the AGF stressed that, in view of the defendant’s confession and the exhibits, he should be convicted on count 4 of the charge, to which he pleaded guilty. The AGF described the offence as very serious, noting that the law prescribes a punishment of at least 20 years’ imprisonment and a maximum of life imprisonment. “I urge my lord to hand down a sentence of not less than 30 years. This is a very serious offence. “If it is not nipped in the bud, a whole generation of our security operatives can be wiped out by people like this providing information about their movement,” the AGF added. He further drew the court’s attention to the fact that count 4 of the charge related to section 13 of the TPPA. The defence counsel, who is from the Legal Aid Council of Nigeria (LACoN), said he was not opposed to the AGF’s submissions. Therefore, Justice Yilwa found the defendant guilty and sentenced him to 40 years in prison, starting from the day of his arrest. The court held that the convict should, upon completing his prison term, be subjected to a rehabilitation and deradicalisation programme. item.title: Africa faces ‘complex’ Ebola outbreak after virus spread to Nigeria – WHO
item.description: The World Health Organization’s Africa chief warned on Thursday that the continent now faced a “complex” Ebola outbreak after the virus crossed from east Africa to Nigeria, which has reported the first case in the west of the continent. “We are facing a more complex outbreak landscape. Nigeria has confirmed an imported case of Ebola virus disease,” Mohamed Janabi, the regional director for WHO in Africa, told an online media briefing. Nigeria on Tuesday announced an imported case of the Bundibugyo strain behind a major DR Congo outbreak, in a woman, a diplomat who had a history of travel to Uganda. The continent’s most populous nation is the fourth African country affected by the outbreak, which this week came to span the continent, with Kenya in the east reporting nine cases since October 6. The case reignited memories of a widespread outbreak in 2014 that struck several countries in the region and killed more than 11,000 people across west Africa between late 2013 and 2016. Nigeria’s experience in successfully containing the Ebola outbreak in 2014 raised confidence that the country can respond effectively to new public health threats. The DRC’s Ebola epidemic has become the deadliest in the country’s history, killing 4,381 people out of more than 9,000 confirmed cases since mid-May, according to the health authorities. item.title: US Embassy issues health alert to Americans in Nigeria amid Bundibugyo Ebola case
item.description: The United States Embassy in Abuja has issued a health alert following Nigeria’s report of a case of Bundibugyo virus disease, a form of Ebola, on October 20, 2026. In the alert published on October 21, the US Mission Nigeria said health officials were conducting contact tracing after the case was reported. According to the alert, the Nigerian Ministry of Health said the affected individual had travelled by air from Uganda. The embassy described Ebola as a serious health concern, stating that “Ebola is a rare, severe, and often fatal hemorrhagic fever illness.” The US Embassy urged travelers to consult health guidance from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and take precautions against possible exposure to the virus. It advised people to visit the CDC’s Ebola information page and its travel health page for Nigeria for relevant information. The embassy also advised people who may be at risk of Ebola to alert their healthcare providers if they experience symptoms consistent with the disease, so they can receive guidance before presenting for medical care. Travellers were further advised to continue taking malaria preventive medication as recommended by their doctors, noting that malaria symptoms can resemble those of Ebola and trigger avoidable health scares. The alert also urged people returning from areas experiencing an Ebola outbreak to monitor their health for 21 days after travel. The US Embassy advised travellers to consult the US Department of State’s Nigeria country page for general health information. It also directed them to the embassy’s list of medical providers and encouraged them to contact their travel insurance providers to understand available medical evacuation options if they become ill while overseas. item.description: The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has warned that it will blacklist partners who fail to account for funds received to combat disease outbreaks on the continent. ﻿ It also warned that the era of organisations operating without transparency is over. Partners will get money from donors. They will implement their activities without disclosing how much they got, without even sending a report to the government,” Kaseya. “And when the outbreak is over, we’ll hear from some capitals that billions of dollars were invested to stop this outbreak. I said, enough is enough. It will never happen again on this continent. “We managed to fundraise. We got figures from all donors. item.title: Court Resumes Trial Of Suspects Linked To Abduction Of NYSC Members, Others In Imo
item.description: Court is set to resume the trial of suspects linked to the abduction of 20 members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) and others in Imo State. The suspects were apprehended in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, and Abia State during intelligence-led operations conducted between October 10 and 14 by the Department of State Services (DSS), in collaboration with the military, police, and other security operatives. Three other suspects reportedly escaped with gunshot wounds, prompting a manhunt for the fleeing members of the gang. The prospective corps members were abducted along the Owerri-Onitsha Expressway in Imo State on October 1, 2026, while they were travelling from Ibadan, Oyo State, to their assigned NYSC orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states. The gunmen attacked two buses conveying the prospective corps members and other passengers near Umunoha in the Mbaitoli Local Government Area of Imo State. The victims were rescued on October 7 during a joint security operation at Amakohia-Ubi Village in Owerri West Local Government Area of the state. They were subsequently taken to the DSS hospital in Owerri for medical attention and necessary checks. During the search-and-rescue operation, the police had said their operatives located the kidnappers’ camp through drone surveillance but could not immediately advance because the location was reportedly planted with improvised explosive devices (IEDs). Security agencies later intensified efforts to reach the victims and secure their release.
